column1: # expect: deny, ask, allow, or pass. The strictest decision of all Bash hooks
# wins. The hooks run in a scratch repository on the branch topic; test/cases.sh
# says which of its branches have a merged pull request.
# Leave out git commit: that hook scans the index of the current repository.
# Force push is denied by permissions.deny (deny.tsv). The hooks ask for it,
# so the forms the rules miss still stop

column2: git status && git push -f origin HEAD

column1: # The hooks do not parse quotes, so a push in a message also asks

column2: git tag -a v1 -m "x; git push -f origin HEAD"

column1: # Only git push origin HEAD from a branch other than main, master, or
# develop goes without asking. The scratch repository is on topic, so the
# main side is not covered here.

column2: git status && git push origin main

column1: # gh api asks when it writes: a method other than GET, or fields without -X GET
# Force-deleting or overwriting a branch asks; git branch -d is allowed
# Chained, git branch is denied for running in the sandbox; see the end
# git branch -D alone is allowed when every branch is the head of a merged
# pull request at the same commit
# A command in sandbox.excludedCommands is denied when chained, since only a
# lone command runs outside the sandbox. Quotes, heredoc bodies, and 2>&1 are
# not read. Missed: sh -c, ( ), $( ), and git -C sub switch

column2: git switch main && git pull origin main
git switch main && git pull origin main && git branch -D topic
for b in a b; do git branch -m $b x$b; done
git tag -a v1 -m "git switch main && git pull origin main"
git tag -a v1 -m 'run git stash; then git stash pop'

git tag -a v1 -F - <<'MSG'
Subject

git switch main && git pull origin main
MSG
gh pr create --title x --body "git pull origin main; git switch main"
